Sonic the Hedgehog. Sega's flagship platformer franchise debuting in 1991, centered on a super-fast blue hedgehog racing through loop-de-loop filled levels to stop the evil scientist Dr. Robotnik. Known for emphasis on speed, momentum-based level design, and a pop-culture aesthetic, the franchise became Sega's mascot and a cultural icon of the nineteen-nineties.

Sonic debuted in 1991 on the Sega Genesis, designed to compete with Nintendo's Mario. Sonic's speed and attitude appealed to older, hipper audiences than Mario's mustachioed plumber. Core design principles emphasize levels designed for high-speed traversal with loops, half-pipes, and enemy lines that reward momentum awareness. Sonic collects rings as a health buffer. Taking damage drops rings, which can be recollected if you're quick. Sonic the Hedgehog 2 in 1992 introduced Tails, Miles Prower, Sonic's flying fox sidekick, and the ability to emerge as Super Sonic, an invulnerable, golden form achieved by collecting Chaos Emeralds.

Sonic 3 and Knuckles in 1994 introduced Knuckles the Echidna, a rival-turned-ally, and expanded Chaos Emerald collection into half-pipe bonus stages. The game's level design sophistication peaked here. The franchise shifted to three-dimensional gameplay with Sonic Adventure in 2001 on Dreamcast, introducing multiple playable characters including Tails, Knuckles, and Big the Cat, each with different play styles. Later three-dimensional entries received mixed reception for experimental mechanics.

Modern entries oscillate between speed-focused design and gimmick-heavy stages. Sonic Mania in 2017 returned to two-dimensional gameplay with original-style level design. Recently, Sonic Frontiers in 2022 introduced open-zone exploration, departing from linear level design. The franchise's tone and mechanical consistency has been historically inconsistent.

Sega is the developer and publisher, and Sonic was Sega's answer to Mario. Tails is Sonic's loyal sidekick and co-protagonist in many entries. Dr. Robotnik, also known as Dr. Eggman, is the mustachioed villain obsessed with capturing Sonic and Tails. Sonic's revolutionary speed-focused level design contrasts sharply with Mario's emphasis on precision platforming.
